company_notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market SaaS (sales/SDR agent product) building outbound chat assistants that can take actions: CRM updates (HubSpot), send emails, schedule calendar invites, call external tools via function calls.
- Primary evaluation: start on Hosted API for speed, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation after sizing tests.
- Top priority: low-latency streaming & tool-calling reliability. Stakeholders repeatedly: VP Product (Marta Alvarez), Head of Sales (Jon Kim), CTO (Arun Desai).
POC details / findings:
- Hosted POC (2 weeks) implemented streaming chat with partial function calling to a staging HubSpot instance and Google Calendar via API glue.
- Observed: median latency comfortably low; tail (p95) exceeded internal SLO (~250ms) during parallel session spikes. Suspect batching + kernel selection could be tuned. SE (Liam) suggested quantization profile + prefix caching.
- Functional accuracy acceptable; tool-call roundtrip reliability ~98% in tests; failure modes: occasional tokenization delays and retry loops when callbacks timed out.
Security & compliance:
- Need SSO (SAML) for admin console access, audit logs retained 1 year, KMS for key separation, and documentation for ISO27001 controls. OrbitVoice legal needs data residency assurances for EU customers.
Commercial + ops:
- Looking at a committed Dedicated pool to support ~50 concurrent active agents (peak 120) — estimate 300 calls/sec during heavy campaigns. Wants predictable per-token costs and an option for burst.
- Quote asked for monthly committed capacity + overage tiers. Early ask: 12-month and 24-month committed options.
Quotes from customers/stakeholders:
- VP Product: "If tool-calling latency is inconsistent we lose agent trust — must be under 250ms for actions."
- Head of Sales: "We need streaming so reps can see partial suggestions and accept/send quickly — no perceptible lag."
Next steps (short):
- Deliver Dedicated demo with throughput and latency tests (Liam to run internal sim harness)
